sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.title: Admin guide
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.subtitle: Everything a guild admin needs to run events: creating matches, managing players, wiring up Discord, and tending the guild itself. The player-facing version of this is at <helpLink>/help</helpLink>.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.createMatch.step1: Go to Manage Events in the sidebar and click + New event.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.createMatch.step2: Pick Match for the event type. Match events have two squads with their own start times, leadership slots, and a backup roster. (Pick Simple for info-only entries like meetings or watch parties — no signups, just a calendar item.)
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.createMatch.step3: Fill in the name, optional description, and the signup window (Signup Opens / Signup Closes). The window is shared by both squads.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.createMatch.step4: Set Squad 1 Starts At and Squad 2 Starts At. Either or both can be left blank — players see "TBD" until you fill them in. Each squad's reminders fire independently from its own start time.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.createMatch.step5: All datetime fields are entered in your browser's local time. The form shows the UTC equivalent below each input so there's no ambiguity. Times are stored as UTC and rendered in each viewer's local zone.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.createMatch.step6: Optional: customize squad names, max players, max backups, and leadership slots. Defaults are 20 / 10 / 3 per squad (60 total slots).
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.createMatch.step7: Click Create Event. You land on the event admin page.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.editEvent.dates: Dates: on the event admin page, click Edit dates. You can change the signup window and both squad start times.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.editEvent.reschedule: Reschedule re-fires reminders: changing any start time clears the "already sent" record for that squad, so the Discord bot will fire fresh 24h / 1h / 20-min reminders against the new time. Tweaking by a couple of minutes also clears them, so avoid nudging unless you mean to re-notify.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.editEvent.softDelete: Soft delete: the Delete Event button hides the event from players but keeps the signup data for attendance reports. Deleted events show up under a separate "Deleted" section on Manage Events.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.managePlayers.intro: The event admin page shows two squad columns and a waitlist below. In each squad column, every signup is a row with these controls:
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.managePlayers.moveSquad: Move to Squad N button: moves the player to the other squad in one click. Updates the assigned squad; if the new squad differs from their first-choice preference, a small MOVED badge appears next to their name so you remember you overrode their preference.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.managePlayers.moveBackup: Move to Backup / Roster button: toggles the player between the main roster (player) and the backup roster (backup). Works in any column, including the waitlist — handy for promoting a waitlister directly to backup.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.managePlayers.roleDropdown: Role dropdown (Unassigned / Player / Backup / Leader / Waitlist): finer-grained role changes. Use this to promote a leadership-requesting player to leader, or to push someone onto the waitlist.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.managePlayers.attendedRating: Attended checkbox + 1-5 star rating: post-event bookkeeping. Both auto-save when toggled. Used for future roster decisions.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.managePlayers.effectiveSquadNo: The squad columns group by effective squad: admin assignment wins, otherwise first-choice preference. So a player you move with Move to Squad 2 immediately appears in the Squad 2 column on the next render.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.managePlayers.leaderPillNote: The Leader yellow pill next to a name means that player asked for a leadership role on signup. Pick leaders from these requests by changing their role to Leader.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.waitlist.intro: When all squad and backup slots are taken, new signups land in the waitlist (assigned role = waitlist). The waitlist section at the bottom of the event admin page shows them in signup order.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.waitlist.promote: To promote someone off the waitlist, change their role from Waitlist to Player or Backup via the dropdown — or use Move to Backup for the common case. Their squad placement comes from their first-choice preference unless you explicitly move them.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.intro: A scrim is a 1-vs-1 guild challenge negotiated between two guild admins, with a single squad on each side. Once accepted, both guilds get a mirrored event that their members can sign up for. After the match either admin declares the result.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.serverNote: Server # is required. Both guilds must have the same Server # set in Guild Settings — otherwise they won't appear in each other's opponent dropdown. Set yours in <settingsLink>Guild Settings</settingsLink> first.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.proposeStep1: Go to the <scrimmagesLink>scrimmages dashboard</scrimmagesLink> and click + Propose scrim.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.proposeStep2: Pick the opponent (filtered to your same Server #), the game time, and the location — either one of the canonical maps (Kruger, Cerno, Kanvo, Sphinx) or a free-text custom location.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.proposeStep3: Fill in the Condition of Win (required). State the rules clearly — both sides see this and it's tied to the declared result. Example: "First team to 3 captures" or "Hold the central fortress for 5 minutes."
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.proposeStep4: Optional message for house rules, format notes, etc. Click Send proposal.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.acceptDeclineHeading: Accept or decline an incoming proposal
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.acceptDeclineIntro: Pending proposals from other guilds show up in the Incoming proposals section of the scrim dashboard.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.accept: Accept creates two mirrored events (one per guild) in a single transaction. Each side's event is named "Scrim vs <opponent>", gets the proposed game time as its start, and accepts member signups like a normal match — except there's only one squad.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.decline: Decline flips the proposal to declined without creating any events.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.withdraw: Withdraw (outgoing only) cancels your own pending proposal before the other side responds.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.rosterBody: The mirrored event lives under Manage Events with a red SCRIM badge. Open it to see your roster — single squad, same admin controls as a match (move to backup, role dropdown, attended, rating). Squad-2 columns and the second start time are hidden because they don't apply.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.cancelBody: Either guild's admin can Cancel from the dashboard while it's in Upcoming scrims and before a result is declared. Cancel soft-deletes both mirrored events (signups are kept for attendance history) and flips the proposal to cancelled.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.resultIntro: Open the scrim event under Manage Events. The result form has four buttons:
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.resultWonLost: We won / We lost — your guild's outcome. The server stores an absolute (perspective-free) result, so the opposing guild sees the inverse W/L automatically.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.resultDrawNc: Draw / No contest — symmetric outcomes. No contest covers forfeits, disconnects, or any scenario where the match didn't complete.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.resultBody: Optional notes are visible to both guilds' members. Once declared, the result shows up as a chip on the event page, the scrim dashboard, and players' scrim history. Either admin can declare — first one to submit wins (no overwrite UI).
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.discordNotificationsBod: If a guild has a Discord channel configured (see below), the bot posts an English message to both guilds' channels on propose / accept / decline. The message includes the opponent name, game time (rendered in each viewer's local timezone), location, and condition of win.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.discordNotificationsFal: If the other guild has a channel configured but the bot can't reach it (bot kicked, channel deleted, wrong ID), you'll see a browser alert listing the affected guild names after your action completes. Guilds without any channel configured stay silent — that's an intentional opt-out.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.scrims.playerVisibilityBody: Players see scrim events on the home page with a red SCRIM badge, can sign up like any match (just one squad to pick), and can browse all accepted scrims (upcoming + past results) on the <scrimsLink>scrim history page</scrimsLink>. Declined, withdrawn, and cancelled proposals are hidden from players — they only see scrims that actually happened or are scheduled.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.inviteBot.intro: Reminders and slash commands rely on a Discord bot the operator already deployed. To wire it up to your Discord server:
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.inviteBot.step1Intro: Get the install URL from your site operator. It looks like:
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.inviteBot.step1Note: The permissions=133120 part covers Send Messages and Mention Everyone. Both are required — without Mention Everyone the @everyone in reminders renders as plain text and doesn't ping anyone.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.inviteBot.step2: Open the install URL in a browser. Pick the Discord server you want the bot in. You need the Manage Server permission in that server. Click Authorize.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.inviteBot.step3: Confirm the bot appears in your Discord server's member list. That's it — no per-bot configuration on the Discord side.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.discordChannel.intro: The bot posts reminders into one channel of your choice. To configure it:
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.discordChannel.step1: Enable Developer Mode in Discord: User Settings → Advanced → Developer Mode. One-time per device. This unlocks the "Copy Channel ID" right-click option.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.discordChannel.step2: Right-click the channel you want reminders in → Copy Channel ID. You'll get a long number like 123456789012345678. Make sure it's a text channel and that the bot's role has View Channel and Send Messages permissions there.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.discordChannel.step3: On the website, go to <settingsLink>Guild Settings</settingsLink> and paste the channel ID into Discord channel ID.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.discordChannel.step4: Click Test integration. If everything is right, you'll see a confirmation in the UI and a one-off test message in the channel. The test step also auto-links your Discord server to the app guild so slash commands (/upcoming, /signup) work.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.discordChannel.step5: Click Save to persist the channel ID.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.discordChannel.commonErrors: Common errors after Test: "Bot doesn't have access to that channel" (re-invite the bot via the install URL above); "Bot is missing the Send Messages permission" (channel-level permission overrides — fix in Discord); "That channel ID doesn't exist" (you copied the server ID, not the channel ID).
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.slashCommands.intro: Once the bot is in the server and you've linked the channel via Test integration, your members can use:
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.slashCommands.upcoming: /upcoming — lists the guild's upcoming events with both squad start times. Replies are ephemeral (only visible to the user).
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.slashCommands.signup: /signup event:<event> squad:<1|2> — signs the user up for an event. The event field has autocomplete. The user has to have signed in to the website with Discord at least once so the bot can match their Discord ID to their guild account — it'll prompt them if they haven't.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.slashCommands.propagation: New global slash commands take up to about 1 hour to propagate the first time after the bot deploys. After that, they're instant.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.slashCommands.failIntro: Usually means Discord cached an outdated version of the command schema, or the bot was added with a missing scope. Try in order:
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.slashCommands.failStep1: Verify scopes and re-invite. The install URL must include both bot and applications.commands scopes. If the bot was added via an older URL that was missing applications.commands, autocomplete events don't reach it. Re-invite using the current install URL (Guild Settings → Discord → Invite Event Organizer Discord Bot).
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.slashCommands.failStep2Intro: Force-clear cached commands (operator only). If re-inviting doesn't fix it, your site operator can wipe Discord's cached command list so the bot re-registers fresh on next startup:
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.slashCommands.failStep2Note: Then restart the bot (e.g. fly machine restart) — the clientReady handler re-registers commands from SLASH_COMMANDS on next boot.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.manageGuild.members: <membersLink>Members</membersLink> — list of everyone in the guild. Per row: Promote a member to admin, Demote an admin to member, or Kick a member out. The last admin can't demote or kick themselves — promote someone else first.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.manageGuild.invites: <invitesLink>Invites</invitesLink> — generate invite links. Each invite can have an optional expiry and a max-use cap (blank = unlimited). Click the URL to copy. Use Revoke to invalidate one. Anyone who hits a valid invite link auto-joins the guild as a member.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.manageGuild.settings: <settingsLink>Guild Settings</settingsLink> — guild name, description, public-discovery toggle, Discord channel ID. The slug is permanent; everything else is editable. Toggling Listed in public discovery off means new members can only join via invite link.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.manageGuild.leave: Leave the guild at the bottom of Settings. Your past signups are soft-deleted (kept for attendance reports). If you're the only admin, you have to promote someone else first.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.playersPage.body: <playersLink>Players</playersLink> shows every guild member with their full signup history: which events they signed up for, squad preferences, attendance, ratings, and leadership notes. Useful for picking leaders, building shortlists, or following up with no-shows.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.troubleshooting.reminders: Reminders aren't firing. Check /api/health — if bot.lastPollStartedAt is more than about 5 minutes behind the current time, the poller is stuck. Super-admins can also POST to /api/admin/bot/poll-now to force a poll cycle.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.troubleshooting.rescheduled: An event was rescheduled and people aren't getting re-notified. Confirm the time actually changed (compare against the previous value). The bot only re-fires kinds whose window is still ahead of the new time — if your new time is 30 minutes from now, only the 20-minute reminder will fire, not the 24-hour one.
sourceSnapshot.adminHelp.troubleshooting.movedSquad: A player got assigned to the wrong squad after I moved them. The MOVED badge means assignment differs from preference. To revert, change their role/squad via the dropdown or use the Move to Squad N button to flip them back.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.title: Welcome to Foundation Event Organizer
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.subtitle: This is where your guild signs up for events — Shadowfront matches, scrims, and anything else the leadership wants on the calendar.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.gettingIn.step1: Sign in with Google or Discord on the home page.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.gettingIn.step2: Join your guild. Most people get in via an invite link from a guild admin. You can also browse public guilds at the <discoveryLink>discovery page</discoveryLink>.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.gettingIn.step3: Once you're in a guild, the home page shows that guild's upcoming events.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.gettingIn.note: You can only be in one guild at a time. To move, leave the current one first.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.eventKinds.match: Match events (Shadowfront and similar) — two squads, each with their own start time, leadership slots, and a starting roster plus backups.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.eventKinds.scrim: Scrim events — a 1-vs-1 challenge between your guild and another guild. Single squad, one start time, and a declared winner when it's over. See the Scrimmage events section below.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.eventKinds.simple: Simple events — info-only entries on the calendar (a meeting, an announcement, a watch party). No signup form; just a date and details.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.signup.intro: Open the event from the home page. The signup form has three things:
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.signup.step1: Squad preference (first choice). Pick the squad you most want to play on. If your first choice is full, admins try to place you on the other.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.signup.step2: Willing to be a backup. On by default. Backups fill in when a starter drops. Uncheck this if you only want to play with a guaranteed starting slot.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.signup.step3: Request a leadership position (optional). Leaders coordinate the squad during the match. Admins assign leaders from the requests; you can leave a short note about why you'd like the role.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.signup.submit: Hit Sign Up. You can come back and change any of these answers up until signups close.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.status.intro: When you look at the squad rosters, you'll see one of these next to each name:
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.status.backup: Backup — on the backup roster; plays only if a starter drops.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.status.leader: Leader — chosen by an admin to lead the squad.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.status.waitlist: Waitlist — all squad and backup slots were full when you signed up. You're promoted automatically if someone drops.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.status.wantsLeader: Wants Leader — a player who asked for the role; an admin will pick from these.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.scrims.intro: A scrim is your guild against another guild. The event page works the same as a match — sign up, pick backup willingness, optionally request leadership — but with a few differences worth knowing:
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.scrims.oneSquad: One squad only. There's no Squad 1 vs Squad 2 pick — your guild fields a single lineup against the opponent.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.scrims.opponent: The opponent is shown at the top of the event page, along with the Condition of Win the two admins agreed on. Read it before the match — it's how the winner gets determined.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.scrims.result: Result chip. Once the match is done and an admin declares the result, you'll see a colored chip on the event page: Won, Lost, Draw, or No contest (for forfeits or disconnects).
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.scrims.history: History. See your guild's upcoming and past scrims on the <scrimsLink>scrim history page</scrimsLink>. W/L is from your guild's perspective.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.scrims.note: Only your guild's admin can propose, accept, or cancel a scrim — you just sign up like any other event. If a scrim is cancelled before it happens, the event disappears from your home page and your signup is hidden (admins still keep the record for attendance history).
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.duels.intro: Duels are 1-vs-1 challenges between two players. They're separate from match events and scrims — no roster, no signup form, just two people agreeing on a time and rules.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.duels.find: Find opponents on the <playersLink>player discovery page</playersLink>. It lists everyone on your same server who has opted into being discoverable. Filter by power tier, guild, or name. Click any player's name to see their full profile — rating, record, and complete duel history.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.duels.powerTier: Each player can set a self-reported power tier from I to XIII on their My Account page. The tier reflects your in-game character progression and helps opponents see if a matchup will be fair. Set yours so others can find you at your level.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.duels.challenge: Click Challenge on a player card to propose a duel. Pick the time, the location (Kruger, Cerno, Kanvo, Sphinx, or a custom map), and the Condition of Win — agree the rules clearly because they're tied to the declared result.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.duels.respond: When someone challenges you, the duel shows up under Incoming challenges on your duels page. You can Accept, Decline, or Edit to counter-propose different terms. The proposer can withdraw at any time before the duel is accepted.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.duels.negotiate: Either player can edit a pending proposal — change the time, location, win condition, or message. Whoever sets the latest terms can't accept their own changes; the other side has to confirm. Counter-proposals can ping-pong until somebody accepts what's on the table.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.duels.result: After the duel, either player declares the result on the duel page: I won, I lost, Draw, or No contest (for forfeits or disconnects). The first player to submit locks it in for both sides. Wins and losses update your ELO rating; no contest counts as a duel but doesn't affect ratings.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.duels.rating: Your ELO rating starts at 1000 and moves up or down depending on the duel result and the opponent's rating. Beating a higher-rated player gains more points; losing to a lower-rated player costs more. Your record (W-L-D) and rating show on your player card.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.duels.leaderboard: Once you've played at least 3 confirmed duels, you appear on the <leaderboardLink>server leaderboard</leaderboardLink> ranked by rating. Top spots get gold/silver/bronze chips. Your own rank shows even when you're outside the top 25.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.duels.reputation: After the duel result is declared, both players can leave a 👍 or 👎 about the opponent. Aggregates appear as a percentage on each player's card once they have at least 5 ratings. One rating per duel, locked after submit.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.duels.history: See your full duel history (upcoming, past, declined, withdrawn, cancelled) on the <duelsLink>duels page</duelsLink>. Result chips show W/L/D/NC from your perspective.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.duels.discordDm: If you've signed in with Discord at least once, the bot can DM you about duel events — incoming challenges, accepted, declined, cancelled, and result-declared. Toggle this in My Account. If you have DMs disabled from server members in your Discord settings, the bot can't reach you.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.duels.privacy: You can turn off duel discoverability in My Account to hide from the discovery page and block incoming challenges. Your guild-internal experience is unaffected.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.reminders.bot: If your guild has the Discord bot set up, the bot posts reminders 1 day, 1 hour, and 20 minutes before each event in your guild's chosen channel.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.reminders.ics: Every event page has a Download .ics link for adding the event to your calendar.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.reminders.slashCommands: Discord slash commands: /upcoming lists your guild's upcoming events, and /signup lets you sign up without leaving Discord. You have to sign in to the website with Discord at least once first, so the bot can match your account.
sourceSnapshot.playerHelp.closed: The form turns into a "Signups are closed" message. Reach out to a guild admin if you need to be added late — they can adjust signups manually.
